title: StockTwits dataset spans 10+ years across 25 companies including FAANG
claim: Researchers collected StockTwits data for over ten years for 25 different companies, including Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google.
support: Historical social media dataset enables temporal analysis of sentiment-price correlations.
mechanism: Accumulation of user messages from financial social network over long time horizon allows pattern identification across market cycles.
assumptions: StockTwits is representative of retail investor sentiment
Data collection was consistent across time period
failure_modes: Platform algorithm changes affecting message visibility

title: FAANG subset yields 514k to 1M+ labeled messages by window
claim: FAANG dataset contains 514,320 records for one-year duration and 1,021,417 records for two-year duration.
support: Sample sizes enable power calculation and overfitting risk assessment.
mechanism: Subset filtering by company symbol and date range reduces full 6.4M dataset to manageable windows.
assumptions: No date gaps or duplicates in filtering

title: Three labeling techniques tested: binary, 2-label, 3-label with neutral
claim: Three labeling approaches: (1) Binary (positive if close > open), (2) 2-label percentage change (positive if >=0.5% increase), (3) 3-label with neutral (-0.5% to +0.5%).
support: Price-based labels reduce annotation bias; enables repeatable methodology.
mechanism: Labeling directly from price moves rather than expert judgment automates dataset creation.
assumptions: Price change is causal for sentiment

title: 2-label percentage change outperforms binary and 3-label across models
claim: 2-label technique outperforms: F1 0.59-0.60 vs binary 0.54-0.58 vs 3-label 0.29-0.41 across all tested models.
support: Label scheme design materially impacts performance; higher threshold increases class separation.
mechanism: 0.5% threshold reduces overlap in message patterns; neutral class adds noise.

title: BERT outperforms FinBERT and FinALBERT on StockTwits labels
claim: BERT: F1 0.59-0.60; FinBERT: 0.53-0.54; FinALBERT: 0.29-0.51 due to smaller pre-training (7.4M vs 2.5B words, 10k vs 125k steps).
support: Large pre-trained models benefit from bigger vocabulary and more training steps; domain-specific insufficient without adequate scale.
mechanism: BERT has larger capacity from bigger pre-training corpus; FinALBERT under-trained.
assumptions: No test-set leakage in F1 computation

title: Naive Bayes within 1% F1 of BERT with 180x faster training
claim: Naive Bayes F1 scores within 1% of BERT (0.58 vs 0.59-0.60) but trains in 5 minutes vs 9 hours for BERT.
support: Simple models cost-effective when target label independent of text semantics; transformers not justified by marginal gains.
mechanism: Naive Bayes computes class probabilities directly; no gradient computation required.

title: FinALBERT achieves high F1 on expert-labeled sentiment data
claim: FinALBERT on FinancialPhraseBank: F1 0.83 (2-label), 0.80 (3-label); vs 0.29-0.51 on price-change labels.
support: FinALBERT excels at sentiment when aligned with transformer strength; fails on price labels (external outcome).
mechanism: Sentiment targets align with transformer semantic understanding; price is external, not text-semantic.
assumptions: PhraseBank representative of target sentiment task
failure_modes: Sentiment not correlated with trading decisions

title: FinALBERT exhibits labeling bias; resolved by hyperparameter alignment
claim: FinALBERT collapsed to positive-only predictions (labeling bias); fixed by setting learning_rate=1e-05, batch_size=32, weight_decay per SST-2 benchmark.
support: Under-trained transformers unstable; hyperparameter-data size coupling critical.
mechanism: Under-trained model + high learning rate causes optimization collapse; weight decay provides regularization.
assumptions: SST-2 hyperparameters appropriate for financial domain

title: 3-label class imbalance degrades performance; 1-year: 46.5% pos, 20.4% neutral
claim: 3-label data: 46.5% positive, 33.1% negative, 20.4% neutral (1-year); yields F1 0.21-0.41 vs 0.54-0.60 for 2-label.
support: Imbalanced labels reduce discrimination; neutral class minority adds noise.
mechanism: Neutral class under-represented; models bias to majority; minority-class metrics suffer.

title: FinALBERT pre-training constrained: 7.4M sentences, 10k steps vs 125k default
claim: FinALBERT pre-trained on 7.4M sentences (450MB), 10k steps vs ALBERT baseline 125k steps; authors attribute subperformance to limited budget.
support: Transformer pre-training requires sufficient budget; under-training leads to poor generalization.
mechanism: Fewer steps = fewer gradient updates; smaller vocabulary from fewer diverse examples.

title: Price-change labels decouple from transformer semantic strength
claim: Transformers underperform on price-change labeling because price (external market outcome) is not text-semantic property; transformer advantage (sequence, domain vocab) irrelevant.
support: Authors: 'transformer models did not help'; BiLSTM+attention also struggled (not sequence-dependent).
mechanism: Transformers optimize for semantic/syntactic understanding; price requires text-price correlation memorization only.
assumptions: Price not predictable from text semantics
Class imbalance is secondary to architecture
failure_modes: Future regime could favor semantic models

title: Prediction threshold 0.75 applied to Apple: precision 0.73, recall 0.92
claim: Apple 2-week test: precision 0.73 for positive class (below 0.75 threshold), recall 0.92; yielded 'Avoid investing' signal.
support: Concrete example of signal generation logic and thresholding in practice.
mechanism: Model outputs softmax probabilities; threshold filters for high-confidence positives; filters false positives.

title: Model correlation does not imply live trading profitability or edge
claim: Study demonstrates same-day price-sentiment correlation and reports metrics; no backtest with entry/exit rules, transaction costs, slippage, position sizing, or risk management.
support: Classification accuracy necessary but insufficient for profitable trading strategy.
mechanism: Model predicts same-day label; ignores costs, latency, portfolio constraints, regime changes.

title: TF-IDF vectorizer outperformed Count Vectorizer in grid search
claim: 5-fold cross-validation grid search found TF-IDF vectorizer superior to Count Vectorizer for all traditional ML models across all labeling schemes.
support: TF-IDF (term frequency-inverse document frequency) better captures word importance than raw counts for financial text.
mechanism: TF-IDF weights words by frequency in document and rarity across corpus; downweights common stop words; Count Vectorizer overweights stop words.
assumptions: Stop words are uninformative for price direction
Word rarity across corpus is meaningful
failure_modes: Domain-specific stop words different from standard list
Financial text may need different preprocessing
validation: Grid search hyperparameter selection reported in Methods

title: Cross-validation minimal improvement over train-test split for traditional models
claim: 5-fold cross-validation provided minimal F1 improvement (<1%) over train-test split for Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, Random Forest; Gradient Boosting performance degraded.
support: Large dataset size (500k+) reduces benefit of cross-validation; single train-test split suffices for stable estimates.
mechanism: With large training set, variance in fold-level estimates low; test-set performance representative.
assumptions: Dataset size large enough to stabilize metrics
Folds stratified to preserve class distribution
failure_modes: Small dataset requires CV for stable estimates
validation: Tables 6-7 compare train-test vs 5-fold CV F1 scores
